title: The Sunday Read: ‘Wikipedia’s Moment of Truth’

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一个关于设计之爱及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 回想一下，在我还在黑胶唱片时代夜店当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带上300件你最珍爱的藏品去上班，然后把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成这样一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面陈列着美丽的50岁老古董。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重塑者》。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm John Gertner.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是约翰·格特纳。

sentences.en: I'm a contributor to The New York Times Magazine, and I write about science and technology.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人，我主要写科学和技术类文章。

sentences.en: This week's Sunday Read is a story I wrote for the magazine about Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 本周的周日阅读是我为该杂志写的一篇关于维基百科的文章。

sentences.en: It's a story that explains how the 22-year-old wonky online encyclopedia we've all consulted at one point is so central to building artificial intelligence right now.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章解释了那个我们都在某个时候查阅过的、22岁略显书呆子气的在线百科全书，是如何在当今构建人工智能中发挥如此核心作用的。

sentences.en: So, over the last few years, computer scientists have been creating what are known as large language models, which are the AI brains, the power, the chatbots, like ChatGPT.
sentences.zh: 所以，在过去的几年里，计算机科学家们一直在创建被称为大语言模型的系统，它们就是人工智能的大脑、驱动力和聊天机器人，比如ChatGPT。

sentences.en: And in order to build a large language model, they needed to gather vast knowledge banks of information.
sentences.zh: 为了构建大语言模型，他们需要收集庞大的知识库信息。

sentences.en: And I mean, it's sort of dizzying how much information we're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在这里谈论的信息量简直让人眼花缭乱。

sentences.en: Some models ingest upwards of a trillion words.
sentences.zh: 有些模型吞噬了超过一万亿个单词。

sentences.en: And it all comes from public sources like Wikipedia or Reddit or Google's patent database.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都来自诸如维基百科、红迪网或谷歌专利数据库等公共来源。

sentences.en: What makes Wikipedia special is not just that it's free and accessible, but also that it's very highly formatted.
sentences.zh: 维基百科的特别之处不仅在于它是免费和可访问的，还在于它有着非常高度结构化的格式。

sentences.en: It contains just a tremendous amount of factual information that's maintained by a community of about 40,000 active editors in the English language version alone.
sentences.zh: 它包含了海量的事实信息，仅英文版就由大约4万名活跃编辑组成的社区进行维护。

sentences.en: The problem with these new AI chatbots is that their fundamental goal is to converse with the user with a kind of human fluency of language,
sentences.zh: 这些新的人工智能聊天机器人存在的问题在于，它们的基本目标是以人类语言的某种流利度与用户对话，

sentences.en: but they're not built to regurgitate data or to really be precise.
sentences.zh: 但它们并不是为了背诵数据或真正做到精确而构建的。

sentences.en: So whether you're trying to understand historical topics or political upheavals or pandemics, these bots greatly simplify the world in a way that's maybe not conducive at all
sentences.zh: 因此，无论你是想了解历史主题、政治动荡还是大流行病，这些机器人都在很大程度上将世界简化了，这可能完全不利于

sentences.en: to our best interests as human beings.
sentences.zh: 我们作为人类的切身利益。

sentences.en: AI chatbots have even been known to hallucinate and conjure falsehoods from whole cloth.
sentences.zh: 人工智能聊天机器人甚至以会产生幻觉和凭空捏造虚假信息而闻名。

sentences.en: And another problem is that if they're fed only on their own synthetic data, these systems essentially break down.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，如果它们仅靠自身生成的合成数据来喂养，这些系统本质上就会崩溃。

sentences.en: So if we were to go to AI instead of Wikipedia to find information, to solve our problems, to answer questions,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们转而向人工智能而不是维基百科来寻找信息、解决问题、回答问题，

sentences.en: what would happen in the future where our knowledge is factually unreliable?
sentences.zh: 那么未来当我们的知识在事实上变得不可靠时，将会发生什么？

sentences.en: As I reported this story, I read a lot of what are called community notes, which are the logs of Wikipedia editor meetings that they transcribe and make public.
sentences.zh: 在我报道这个故事时，我阅读了许多所谓的社区记录，也就是维基百科编辑会议的日志，他们将这些会议记录转录并公之于众。

sentences.en: And in one recent meeting, editors shared their worries about AI.
sentences.zh: 在最近的一次会议上，编辑们分享了他们对人工智能的担忧。

sentences.en: What's it going to do to Wikipedia?
sentences.zh: 这会对维基百科产生什么影响？

sentences.en: I remember reading the notes for this meeting, and one line from an editor popped out at me.
sentences.zh: 我记得在阅读这次会议的记录时，一位编辑的一句话跃入我的眼帘。

sentences.en: We want a future where knowledge is created by humans.
sentences.zh: 我们想要一个由人类创造知识的未来。

sentences.en: And I thought, well, that's really the essence of it, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想，这确实是它的精髓所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: Can we really choose at this point the future we want?
sentences.zh: 在这个时候，我们真的能选择我们想要的未来吗？

sentences.en: So here's my article, Wikipedia's Moment of Truth, read by Brian Nishi.
sentences.zh: 以下是我的文章《维基百科的真理时刻》，由布莱恩·西希朗读。

sentences.en: In early 2021, a Wikipedia editor peered into the future and saw what looked like a funnel cloud on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 2021年初，一位维基百科编辑凝视着未来，看到地平线上出现了一个看起来像漏斗云的东西。

sentences.en: The rise of GPT-3, a precursor to the new chatbots from OpenAI.
sentences.zh: GPT-3的崛起，它是OpenAI新聊天机器人的前身。

sentences.en: When this editor, a prolific Wikipedian who goes by the handle Barkeep49 on the site, gave the new technology a try, he could see that it was untrustworthy.
sentences.zh: 当这位编辑——一位在网站上使用Barkeep49这个网名的多产维基人——尝试了这项新技术时，他看出它是不可信的。

sentences.en: The bot would readily mix fictional elements, a false name, a false academic citation, into otherwise factual and coherent answers.
sentences.zh: 这个机器人会轻易地将虚构的元素（假名字、假学术引文）混入原本充满事实和连贯的回答中。

sentences.en: But he had no doubts about its potential.
sentences.zh: 但他对它的潜力没有任何怀疑。

sentences.en: I think AI's day of writing a high-quality encyclopedia is coming sooner rather than later, he wrote in Death of Wikipedia,
sentences.zh: 他写道：我认为人工智能编写高质量百科全书的日子指日可待。他在《维基百科之死》中写道，

sentences.en: an essay that he posted under his handle on Wikipedia itself.
sentences.zh: 这是一篇他在维基百科上以自己的网名发表的文章。

sentences.en: He speculated that a computerized model could, in time, displace his beloved website and its human editors, just as Wikipedia had supplanted the Encyclopedia Britannica,
sentences.zh: 他推测，随着时间的推移，计算机模型可能会取代他挚爱的网站及其人类编辑，正如当年维基百科取代《大英百科全书》一样，

sentences.en: which in 2012 announced it was discontinuing its print publication.
sentences.zh: 后者在2012年宣布停止纸质版出版。

sentences.en: Recently, when I asked this editor, he asked me to withhold his name because Wikipedia editors can be the targets of abuse, if he still worried about his encyclopedia's fate.
sentences.zh: 最近，当我问这位编辑（他要求我隐去他的名字，因为维基百科编辑可能会成为攻击的目标）他是否仍然担心他的百科全书的命运时，

sentences.en: He told me that the newer versions made him more convinced that ChatGPT was a threat.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，更新的版本让他更加确信ChatGPT是一个威胁。

sentences.en: It wouldn't surprise me if things are fine for the next three years, he said of Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果接下来三年一切正常，我也不会感到惊讶，他在谈到维基百科时说。

sentences.en: And then, all of a sudden, in year four or five, things drop off a cliff.
sentences.zh: 然后，突然之间，在第四年或第五年，情况就会一落千丈。

sentences.en: Wikipedia marked its 22nd anniversary in January.
sentences.zh: 维基百科在1月迎来了它的22周年纪念日。

sentences.en: It remains, in many ways, a throwback to the Internet's utopian early days, when experiments with open collaboration, anyone can write and edit for Wikipedia,
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，它仍然是互联网乌托邦早期的一个复古产物，当时开放协作的实验（任何人都可以为维基百科撰写和编辑）

sentences.en: had yet to cede the digital terrain to multibillion-dollar corporations and data miners, advertising schemers and social media propagandists.
sentences.zh: 尚未将数字领地拱手让给数十亿美元的巨头、数据挖掘者、广告策划者和社交媒体说客。

sentences.en: The goal of Wikipedia, as its co-founder Jimmy Wales described it in 2004, was to create a world in which every single person on the planet
sentences.zh: 正如其联合创始人吉米·威尔斯在2004年所描述的那样，维基百科的目标是创造这样一个世界：地球上的每一个人

sentences.en: is given free access to the sum of all human knowledge.
sentences.zh: 都可以免费获得人类知识的总和。

sentences.en: The following year, Wales also stated, we help the Internet not suck.
sentences.zh: 第二年，威尔斯还表示，我们让互联网不那么糟糕。

sentences.en: Wikipedia now has versions in 334 languages and a total of more than 61 million articles.
sentences.zh: 维基百科现在拥有334种语言的版本，总共拥有超过6100万篇文章。

sentences.en: It consistently ranks among the world's 10 most visited websites, yet is alone among that select group, whose usual leaders are Google, YouTube, and Facebook,
sentences.zh: 它一直名列全球访问量最大的前10个网站之列，但在这些通常由谷歌、YouTube和脸书领衔的精选群体中，它是唯一一个

sentences.en: in eschewing the profit motive.
sentences.zh: 摒弃营利动机的网站。

sentences.en: Wikipedia does not run ads, except when it seeks donations, and its contributors, who make about 345 edits per minute on the site, are not paid.
sentences.zh: 维基百科不投放广告（除非在寻求捐款时），其贡献者（他们在该网站上每分钟进行约345次编辑）是没有任何报酬的。

sentences.en: In seeming to repudiate capitalism's imperatives, its success can seem surprising, even mystifying.
sentences.zh: 在看似抗拒资本主义指令的同时，它的成功可能显得令人惊奇，甚至神秘莫测。

sentences.en: Some Wikipedians remark that their endeavor works in practice, but not in theory.
sentences.zh: 一些维基人评论说，他们的事业在实践中行之有效，但在理论上却行不通。

sentences.en: Wikipedia is no longer an encyclopedia, or at least not only an encyclopedia.
sentences.zh: 维基百科不再只是一部百科全书，或者至少不仅仅是一部百科全书。

sentences.en: Over the past decade, it has become a kind of factual netting that holds the whole digital world together.
sentences.zh: 在过去的十年里，它已经变成了一种将整个数字世界维系在一起的事实网络。

sentences.en: The answers we get from searches on Google and Bing, or from Siri and Alexa, how old is Joe Biden, or what is an ocean submersible, derive in part from Wikipedia's data
sentences.zh: 我们从谷歌和Bing搜索中，或者从Siri和Alexa那里得到的答案（例如乔·拜登多大年龄，或者什么是海洋潜水器），部分来自于维基百科的数据

sentences.en: having been ingested into their knowledge banks.
sentences.zh: 被吸收进它们的知识库中。

sentences.en: YouTube has also drawn on Wikipedia to counter misinformation.
sentences.zh: YouTube也利用维基百科来打击虚假信息。

sentences.en: The new AI chatbots have typically swallowed
sentences.zh: 新的人工智能聊天机器人通常也已经吞噬了

sentences.en: Wikipedia's corpus, too.
sentences.zh: 维基百科的语料库。

sentences.en: Embedded deep within their responses to queries is Wikipedia data and Wikipedia text, knowledge that has been compiled over years of painstaking work by human contributors.
sentences.zh: 深深嵌入它们对查询的回答中的是维基百科的数据和维基百科的文本，这些知识是人类贡献者经过多年艰苦工作编译而成的。

sentences.en: While estimates of its influence can vary,
sentences.zh: 虽然对其影响的估计可能有所不同，

sentences.en: Wikipedia is probably the most important single source in the training of AI models.
sentences.zh: 但维基百科可能是训练人工智能模型中最单一最重要的来源。

sentences.en: Without Wikipedia, generative AI wouldn't exist, says Nicholas Vincent, who will be joining the faculty of Simon Fraser University in British Columbia this month,
sentences.zh: 没有维基百科，生成式人工智能就不会存在，尼古拉斯·文森特说，他将于本月加入不列颠哥伦比亚省西蒙弗雷泽大学的教职，

sentences.en: and who has studied how Wikipedia helps support
sentences.zh: 他一直研究维基百科如何支持

sentences.en: Google searches and other information businesses.
sentences.zh: 谷歌搜索和其他信息业务。

sentences.en: Yet, as bots like ChatGPT become increasingly popular and sophisticated,
sentences.zh: 然而，随着像ChatGPT这样的机器人变得越来越受欢迎和复杂，

sentences.en: Vincent and some of his colleagues wonder what will happen if Wikipedia, outflanked by AI that has cannibalized it, suffers from disuse and dereliction.
sentences.zh: 文森特和他的一些同事想知道，如果被其吞噬的人工智能超越的维基百科因无人问津而荒废，将会发生什么。

sentences.en: In such a future, a death-of-Wikipedia outcome outcome is perhaps not so far-fetched.
sentences.zh: 在这样的未来，维基百科消亡的结果或许并非遥不可及。

sentences.en: A computer intelligence, it might not need to be as good as Wikipedia, merely good enough, is plugged into the web and seizes the opportunity to summarize source materials
sentences.zh: 一种计算机智能，它可能不需要像维基百科那样好，只要足够好就行，它接入网络并抓住机会即时总结源材料

sentences.en: and news articles instantly, the way humans now do with argument and deliberation.
sentences.zh: 和新闻文章，就像人类现在通过争论和审议所做的那样。

sentences.en: On a conference call in March that focused on AI's threats to Wikipedia, as well as the potential benefits, the editors' hopes contended with anxiety.
sentences.zh: 在3月份的一次电话会议上，重点讨论了人工智能对维基百科的威胁以及潜在的好处，编辑们的希望与焦虑交织在一起。

sentences.en: While some participants seemed confident that generative AI tools would soon help expand
sentences.zh: 虽然一些参与者似乎坚信生成式人工智能工具很快将有助于扩大

sentences.en: Wikipedia's articles and global reach, others worried about whether users would increasingly choose
sentences.zh: 维基百科的文章和全球影响力，但另一些人则担心用户是否会越来越多地选择

sentences.en: ChatGPT, fast, fluent, seemingly oracular, over a wonky entry from Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 快速、流利、看似神谕般的ChatGPT，而不是维基百科那篇略显书呆子气的条目。

sentences.en: A main concern among the editors was how Wikipedians could defend themselves from such a threatening technological interloper.
sentences.zh: 编辑们主要关心的一个问题是，维基人如何能够保护自己免受这种具有威胁性的技术入侵者的侵害。

sentences.en: And some worried about whether the digital realm had reached a point where their own organization, especially in its striving for accuracy and truthfulness, was being threatened
sentences.zh: 还有一些人担心数字领域是否已经到了这样一个地步：他们自己的组织，尤其是在追求准确性和真实性方面，正受到

sentences.en: by a type of intelligence that was both factually unreliable and hard to contain.
sentences.zh: 一种既在事实上不可靠又难以控制的智能类型的威胁。

sentences.en: One conclusion from the conference call was clear enough.
sentences.zh: 电话会议得出的一个结论已经足够清晰。

sentences.en: We want a world in which knowledge is created by humans.
sentences.zh: 我们想要一个由人类创造知识的世界。

sentences.en: But is it already too late for that?
sentences.zh: 但现在这一切是不是已经太迟了？

sentences.en: Back in 2017, the Wikimedia Foundation and its community of volunteers began exploring how the encyclopedia and its sister sites, like Wikidata and Wikimedia Commons,
sentences.zh: 早在2017年，维基媒体基金会及其志愿者社区就开始探索该百科全书及其姊妹网站（如维基数据和维基共享资源）

sentences.en: with their offerings of free information and images, could evolve by the year 2030.
sentences.zh: 凭借其提供的免费信息和图像，如何在2030年之前实现演变。

sentences.en: The plan was to ensure that the foundation, the non-profit that oversees Wikipedia, could protect and share the world's information in perpetuity.
sentences.zh: 该计划旨在确保监督维基百科的非营利组织基金会能够永远保护和分享世界的讯息。

sentences.en: One outcome of that 2017 effort, which included a year's worth of meetings, was a prediction that Wikimedia would become the essential infrastructure of the ecosystem
sentences.zh: 2017年那次包括了为期一年的会议在内的努力产生的一个结果是，预测维基媒体将成为

sentences.en: of free knowledge.
sentences.zh: 自由知识生态系统的必不可少的基础设施。

sentences.en: Another conclusion was that trends like online misinformation would soon require far more vigilance.
sentences.zh: 另一个结论是，诸如网络虚假信息之类的趋势很快将需要更高水平的警惕。

sentences.en: And a research paper commissioned by the foundation found that artificial intelligence was improving at a rate that could change the way that knowledge is gathered, assembled,
sentences.zh: 基金会委托的一份研究报告发现，人工智能正以惊人的速度发展，这可能会改变收集、汇编

sentences.en: and synthesized.
sentences.zh: 和综合知识的方式。

sentences.en: For that reason, the rollout of ChatGPT did not elicit surprise inside the Wikipedia community, though several editors told me they were shocked by the speed of its adoption,
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，ChatGPT的推出并没有在维基百科社区内部引起惊讶，尽管几位编辑告诉我，他们对它被采用的速度感到震惊，

sentences.en: which needed just two months after its release in late 2022 to gain an estimated
sentences.zh: 它在2022年底发布后仅用了两个月时间就获得了估计

sentences.en: 100 million users.
sentences.zh: 1亿用户。

sentences.en: Despite its stodgy appearance,
sentences.zh: 尽管外表古板，

sentences.en: Wikipedia is more tech-savvy than casual users might assume.
sentences.zh: 但维基百科比普通用户想象的要精通技术得多。

sentences.en: With a small group of volunteers to oversee millions of articles, it has long been necessary for highly experienced editors, often known as administrators, to use semi-automated
sentences.zh: 由于只有一小群志愿者来监督数百万篇文章，经验丰富的编辑（通常被称为管理员）长期以来一直有必要使用半自动化

sentences.en: software to identify misspellings and catch certain forms of intentional misinformation.
sentences.zh: 软件来识别拼写错误并捕捉某些形式的故意虚假信息。

sentences.en: And because of its open-source ethos, the organization has at times incorporated technology made freely available by tech companies or academics, rather than go through a lengthy
sentences.zh: 由于其开源精神，该组织有时会整合科技公司或学者免费提供的技术，而不是经历漫长

sentences.en: and expensive development process on its own.
sentences.zh: 且昂貴的自主开发过程。

sentences.en: We've had artificial intelligence tools and bots since 2002, and we've had a team dedicated to machine learning since
sentences.zh: 我们从2002年起就有了人工智能工具和机器人，我们甚至拥有一个自

sentences.en: Selina Dekelman,
sentences.zh: 起就专注于机器学习的团队，

sentences.en: Wikimedia's chief technology officer, told me.
sentences.zh: 维基媒体的首席技术官塞利娜·德克尔曼

sentences.en: They're extremely valuable for semi-automated content review and especially for translations.
sentences.zh: 对我说。
